subject.title: Version committed server-side after client 120s timeout is stuck hidden (versions:0, updatedAt frozen ~29h) — @borglife/plugin@0.2.1-beta.1

question: Should maintainers first recover this specific hidden version and then prioritize a general owner-visible retry/cancel and worker-recovery design for staged publishes?
rationale: A package-specific server-side state intervention and the permanent transaction/recovery contract require access to production state and maintainer ownership judgment.

options.title: Recover and investigate
options.body: Recommended: inspect the affected package-version and scan-job records, recover or clear the orphaned attempt, and use the result to define the narrow durable fix.

options.title: Treat as a general publish-flow project
options.body: Prioritize a broader owner-visible pending-publish, retry, and cancellation workflow before intervening on individual package records.

options.title: Close after manual recovery only
options.body: Recover this package operationally but defer a product-level recovery surface until another confirmed recurrence.

recommendation.title: Recover and investigate
recommendation.body: Recommended: inspect the affected package-version and scan-job records, recover or clear the orphaned attempt, and use the result to define the narrow durable fix.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged timeout-path work is the strongest available code-history connection to the client deadline involved in this report.
